What exact wire spellings and values do these constants hold, including header-name casing, authorization syntax, answer media type and accepted/rendered UTC marker?
What exact header names and form media type do these constants hold, and does the content-security-policy constant name a header or its complete policy value?

judgement.why: Exact header spellings, media types, authorization syntax, emitted UTC marker and CSP value are wire-format and constant-value details owned by State 6, not State 3 module ownership.

topics.topic: Operations' permitted given_values dependencies and ownership of text-to-typed-value conversion
questions: Which raw texts may operations read through given_values without violating operations' prohibition on owning transport or wire format, and which reader/checker exports does it call?

Which values does operations read through given_values, given that operations must not own transport or wire format, and which module converts owner-form and service-request text into typed operation values?

quotes:
A create or a correction carries its
  values as given (`GivenCustomerFacts`, `GivenProjectFacts`,
  `GivenPointer`); the record's module reads and checks them through
  `given_values` (A02) and turns them into the model's types itself
  (`_object_from_given`). A choice from a closed list arrives as text too, so
  that a value outside it is refused (A19 rule 3) rather than unreadable.

Every text form is read the same way, in `given_values` (owner,
2026-11-26): `module_internal["configuration"]["given_values"]` holds
`read_listen_address`, `module_internal["backups"]["given_values"]`
`read_instant_text` and `module_internal["operations"]["given_values"]`
`read_date_text`, each that one symbol;
`module_internal["migration_import"]["given_values"]` holds
`read_instant_text` and `read_digits_text` beside the readings it already
holds; and `imports.internal["given_values"]` exports the four.
judgement.why: The later dependency graph limits operations to read_date_text, leaves ordinary given fact parsing to record modules, and assigns transport decoding to the surface modules.

topics.topic: Ownership and authority of the OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS subject-kind mapping
questions: Which module owns the new decision that maps each owner action, customer transition and project-erasure kind to its AuditSubjectKind, and is OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS the authoritative mapping rather than a value derived independently by operations or audit_log?
Does data_provider own both the audit action and AuditSubjectKind selected for every OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row, or does another module derive the subject kind independently?

quotes:
A row of the owner audit table: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted
owner action writes — for a customer mark, by its transition; for a project's
erasure, by its kind (owner, 2026-11-24) — and the form of that entry's
subject (M15–M19; owner, 2026-11-26).

Facts: the owner action; the customer mark's transition, where the action has
one; the project erasure's kind, where the action has one; the audit action it
writes; the kind of its entry's subject.
The release: the data provider's `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`.

A14 rules 1 and 5:
appending the audit entry in the action's transaction when the action changed
state, its action the row of the data provider's `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` for
an owner action (owner, 2026-11-24).
judgement.why: State 1 makes both audit action and subject kind fields of the authoritative data_provider row, and State 3 directs operations to use that row when appending the entry.

topics.topic: Runtime-settings collection membership, ordering, and schema ownership
questions: What settings are members of each collection, what order is normative, and does data_provider or runtime_settings own this schema?
Which exact setting identifiers and order these constants contain, how owner-only startup changes required membership, and whether configuration or runtime_settings owns the grouping semantics?

judgement.why: The collections' exact setting identifiers, order and group representation are configuration-schema and constant-value details assigned to State 6; State 3 already assigns environment reading to runtime_settings and ordered checking to configuration.

topics.topic: Store companion suffixes and their handling across creation, cleanup, and backup
questions: Which suffixes are included, for which SQLite modes or operations, and which module decides how companion files are handled during store creation, backup and cleanup?
Which file suffixes are store companions, what operations may create or remove them, and whether they participate in path separation, startup cleanup and backup snapshots?

quotes:
`store.discard_new_store` answers `DiscardResult`: `removed` is true when
  the store's pathname no longer names a file, and `failure` names the first
  step that failed — closing the connection, a companion `-wal`, `-shm` or
  `-journal`, or the store file — with its kind. The steps run in that order
  and stop at the first failure (State 5).

_run_backup: [BEHAVIOR] The run's backup step MUST have copy_store_snapshot copy registry_store to a new temporary path, take the key give_backup_key gives, make the BackupRecord from the imported BACKUP_RECORD_VERSION constant, the StoreSnapshot's fixed_at as its made_at and its last_sequence_number, the imported RELEASE_VERSION constant and _key_digest of the key, write _encrypt_backup of the copy's bytes into a second new temporary file, and remove the unencrypted copy, with each companion file whose path is the copy's path followed by a suffix of the imported STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES constant, before going on; when copy_store_snapshot answers SnapshotFailed, the step MUST remove what it wrote at that path before it reports.
judgement.why: The later contracts fix the companion suffixes as `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal`, their removal order, store ownership and backup-copy cleanup behavior.

topics.topic: Backups' direct given_values dependencies versus hidden backup-format parsing
questions: Which backup text is read by given_values rather than by backups' hidden backup-file-format mechanism, and which given_values symbols does backups import?

topics.topic: Configuration's direct given_values dependencies and post-parsing checks
questions: Which given_values exports does configuration directly use, and which configuration checks remain its own after parsing?

quotes:
Every text form is read the same way, in `given_values` (owner,
2026-11-26): `module_internal["configuration"]["given_values"]` holds
`read_listen_address`, `module_internal["backups"]["given_values"]`
`read_instant_text` and `module_internal["operations"]["given_values"]`
`read_date_text`, each that one symbol;

load_configuration: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST judge an address item well formed exactly when read_listen_address answers a ListenAddress for its text, and MUST put that ListenAddress into its LoadedConfiguration, parsing no address in any other way.
judgement.why: The later dependency graph gives configuration only read_listen_address, while configuration retains presence, grouping, port, secret, distinctness and path checks after parsing.

topics.topic: Migration_import's direct versus indirect dependency on given_values
questions: Must migration_import directly know given_values to read imported instants and version digits, or does another module parse those values before migration_import receives them?

quotes:
`module_internal["migration_import"]["given_values"]` holds
`read_instant_text` and `read_digits_text` beside the readings it already
holds; and `imports.internal["given_values"]` exports the four.

For each request with picks, names, aliases and
   Customer values, `capability:owner_sessions.read_uploaded_file` gives the
   kept file, and `capability:migration_import.read_import_mapping` reads, in
   `capability:store.read_in_transaction`, what the picks bring in and
   nothing else (rule 3): their rooms and pointers, each name and alias they
   arrive under, the Customers it will make, the malformed records (rule 4,
   an undeclared type among them, A22 rule 7, and an instant or a version
   that `capability:given_values.read_instant_text` or
   `capability:given_values.read_digits_text` does not read) and every id production holds
   (rule 5).
judgement.why: The later dependency graph and import flow explicitly make migration_import the direct consumer of read_instant_text and read_digits_text.
